hook_text: Your grandmother carried water in clay. You carry it in plastic. That swap changed the world.
clip_script: Walk into a kitchen from fifty years ago. Clay water pot, enamel bowl, wooden spoon, sisal rope. Now walk into one today. Plastic bucket, stainless steel pot, silicone spatula, nylon rope. Why the swap? Every natural material has a weak spot. Clay smashes. Wood rots and burns. Cotton stays wet. Leather cracks. Thatch leaks and catches fire. So people built materials without the weak spot. Polythene does not rot, rust or smash. Stainless steel does not rust because of chromium. Plywood does not warp because the grain is crossed. Nylon dries in minutes. The result: lighter buckets carried further, pipes that brought clean water to villages, helmets that do not crack, houses built in weeks. That is the positive impact of technology. The cost of all that plastic? That is next week.
visual_style: Split whiteboard: left side sketches of clay pot, wooden spoon, sisal rope; right side their modern replacements appearing one by one with a one-word benefit under each.
pacing: Old kitchen, weak spots, new materials, benefits, cliffhanger about costs.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three objects at home whose natural material was replaced, and name the material.
